summary: The create-monster scroll reaches read.c:seffect_create_monster, but js/read.js records an unported gap. C makes its extra-monster rn2(73) draw before calling create_critters; the missing draw is the first RNG difference at step 30, and the final inventory screen also differs. Port the whole effect and use the existing create_critters Boolean result to set scroll knowledge.

source.branch: read.c:seffect_create_monster (1606-1623) computes count in C evaluation order: one base creature, twelve extra for confusion or curse, and for an unblessed ordinary state rn2(73) followed by optional rnd(4). It passes acid blob species only when confused, calls makemon.c:create_critters, and sets known only when that consumed Boolean is true.
callers: read.c:seffects SCR_CREATE_MONSTER and SPE_CREATE_MONSTER dispatch to seffect_create_monster; js/read.js:seffects currently notes the gap for both.
read.c:doread and spell.c:spelleffects reach the scroll and spell dispatch paths.
dependencies: makemon.c:create_critters is already ported in js/makemon.js and returns a Boolean; use its return value and preserve the wizard-mode prompt behavior.
Keep the rn2(73)/rnd(4) order and gk.known update exactly as C.

evidence: Saved challenges/evaluations/20260927191056-v8.json at 5b4486322ffa5eeb91cc37d01083ff20bbfe2ea7 measures 30/31 screens and 2413/2414 RNG calls; first C RNG at mismatch is rn2(73)=44 from seffect_create_monster(read.c:1616).
Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c defines seffect_create_monster with all branches described above; js/read.js dispatch records note_unported for the same source function.
The selected v8 case's setup and first mismatch are independent C recording evidence; port the full function and both production dispatch arms rather than keying behavior to this case.
